gold.historyOfPresentIllness: The patient is a 36-year-old male presenting with a 4-day history of upper respiratory symptoms. Illness began with congestion and a productive cough with phlegm, accompanied by a fever 2 days ago that has since resolved. He now reports persistent nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, postnasal drainage, and a productive cough, along with a significant frontal sinus headache. He denies current fever.

instructions:
You have a sinus and upper respiratory infection. This is most likely caused by a virus, which is the usual cause in the first days of this kind of illness. Most people get better on their own within about 7 to 10 days. Because of this, antibiotics are not started right away — they are only needed if you are not improving or you get worse.

Your medicines

Fluticasone propionate nasal spray — Use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily for 7–14 days. This reduces swelling and congestion in your nose and sinuses.
Ipratropium bromide nasal spray — Use 2 sprays in each nostril 2–3 times daily for up to 4 days. This helps dry up a runny nose and drainage.
Amoxicillin-clavulanate (antibiotic) — Take by mouth twice daily for 5–7 days. Do not start this right away. Only begin the antibiotic if, after 5–7 days, your symptoms are still not improving or are getting worse. If you clearly improve on your own, you do not need it.
Things that help you feel better

Rinse your nose with saline (saltwater) spray or rinses.
Drink plenty of fluids and rest.
Use acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain or headache, as directed on the package.
Follow-up

If you start the antibiotic and your symptoms have not resolved after 5 days on it, come back for a follow-up visit.

Come back sooner or seek urgent care if you have any of the following:

Swelling, redness, or pain around the eyes
Changes in your vision or double vision
A severe headache, stiff neck, or confusion
A high fever that returns or will not go away
Trouble breathing or chest pain
Symptoms lasting longer than 10 days without any improvement, or symptoms that improved and then suddenly got worse
